title: Staff roster
story: Ada from HR at Contoso asks how many people sit in each department. There is no system yet, so you build the list yourself and keep it safe in git.
result: A git repo with staff.csv, a PowerShell check and a Python head-count script, in two commits.

stages.title: Make the workspace
steps: Open Terminal and make the folder ~/megalab/ops/staff-roster/ in one command.
cd into ~/megalab/ops/staff-roster/ and confirm where you are.
Create an empty file called notes.txt.
List the folder, hidden files included, in long format.
hints: `mkdir -p` makes every missing folder on the way.
stages.expect: pwd prints /Users/<you>/megalab/ops/staff-roster and ls -la shows ., .. and notes.txt.

stages.title: Write staff.csv
steps: Start pwsh inside the staff-roster folder.
Write six lines to staff.csv with Set-Content: header Name,Dept then Ada,IT  Bram,Sales  Lien,IT  Noor,Helpdesk  Jonas,Sales  Mira,IT.
Read it back with Import-Csv into $staff.
Print $staff.Count and the Name of the last row.
hints: `'Name,Dept','Ada,IT' | Set-Content staff.csv` writes one line per string.
The last item of a list is index `-1`.
stages.expect: $staff.Count shows 6 and $staff[-1].Name shows Mira.

stages.title: Filter in PowerShell
steps: Pipe $staff into Where-Object to keep only Dept IT.
Count the result.
Sort all names alphabetically and show only the first 2.
stages.expect: The IT count is 3. The first two sorted names are Ada and Bram.

stages.title: Head count in Python
steps: Create ~/megalab/ops/staff-roster/count.py in VS Code.
Read staff.csv into a list of lines and skip the header line.
Loop over the lines, split each one on the comma and add 1 to a dict per department.
Print every department with its count, one per line, as Dept: n.
Run it with python3 count.py.
hints: `lines = open("staff.csv").read().splitlines()` gives you the lines; `lines[1:]` skips the header.
stages.expect: Three lines in this order: IT: 3, Sales: 2, Helpdesk: 1.

stages.title: Track it with git
steps: Run git init in the staff-roster folder.
Stage staff.csv and commit it with the message add staff list.
Stage count.py and notes.txt and commit with the message add head count.
Show the history in one line per commit.
stages.expect: git log --oneline shows two commits, add head count on top, and git status says nothing to commit, working tree clean.

title: Ticket triage
story: Bram runs the helpdesk and gets a raw ticket log every week. He wants to know which site and which topic cause the most work.
result: tickets.log, a Python converter that writes tickets.csv, a tickets.db SQLite database and two saved report queries.

stages.title: Inspect the raw log
steps: Make ~/megalab/ops/ticket-triage/ and cd into it.

Create tickets.log in VS Code with these 8 lines (date site prio topic): 2026-10-01 GENT P2 printer / 2026-10-01 BRUG P1 network / 2026-10-02 GENT P3 password / 2026-10-02 ANTW P2 printer / 2026-10-03 GENT P1 network / 2026-10-03 BRUG P3 password / 2026-10-04 GENT P2 Printer / 2026-10-04 ANTW P3 laptop
Count the lines that mention GENT.
Count the lines that mention printer, ignoring case.
stages.expect: grep for GENT gives 4. The case-insensitive printer count gives 3 (one line says Printer).

stages.title: Convert log to CSV
steps: Create ~/megalab/ops/ticket-triage/to_csv.py.
Open tickets.log for reading and tickets.csv for writing, both with a with-block.
Write the header row date,site,prio,topic.
For every log line, split it into its four parts and write them as a row, with topic in lower case.
Run it and open tickets.csv in VS Code.
hints: Open the output with `newline=""` so no blank lines appear between rows.
stages.expect: tickets.csv has 9 lines: the header plus 8 rows, and row 8 reads 2026-10-04,GENT,P2,printer.

stages.title: Load into SQLite
steps: Open the database with sqlite3 tickets.db.
Import the CSV as a table called tickets.
Check the row count.
List only the P1 tickets.
hints: `.import --csv tickets.csv tickets` uses the header row as column names.
`.headers on` and `.mode column` make results easier to read.
stages.expect: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tickets; returns 8. The P1 query returns 2 rows, both network (BRUG and GENT).

stages.title: Write the report queries
steps: Create ~/megalab/ops/ticket-triage/report.sql in VS Code.
Query 1: tickets per site, busiest first, ties sorted by site name.
Query 2: tickets per topic, busiest first, ties sorted by topic.
Run the file with sqlite3 tickets.db < report.sql.
hints: `GROUP BY site ORDER BY n DESC, site` where n is `COUNT(*) AS n`.
stages.expect: With the default list mode the output is GENT|4, ANTW|2, BRUG|2 then printer|3, network|2, password|2, laptop|1.

title: License ledger
story: Lien from Finance at Contoso wants the monthly Microsoft 365 cost per department and asks if any license type is paid for but unused.
result: seats.csv from PowerShell, a licenses.db with seats and prices tables, and a PHP page served locally that shows cost per department.

stages.title: Export the seat list
steps: Create ~/megalab/ops/license-ledger/seats.ps1.
Build an array of 8 [PSCustomObject] rows with Name, Dept, Sku: Ada IT E5, Bram Sales BP, Lien IT BP, Noor Helpdesk F3, Jonas Sales BP, Mira IT E5, Tom Helpdesk F3, Eva Sales BP.
Export them to seats.csv without type info.
Run ./seats.ps1, then Import-Csv seats.csv and count the rows.
stages.expect: seats.csv starts with "Name","Dept","Sku" and Import-Csv gives 8 rows.

stages.title: Build the price list
steps: Create ~/megalab/ops/license-ledger/prices.sql.
Create a table prices with sku TEXT PRIMARY KEY and price INTEGER.
Insert E5 57, E3 36, BP 22, F3 8 in one INSERT.
Run sqlite3 licenses.db < prices.sql, then import seats.csv as a table called seats.
hints: Run prices.sql only once: a second run fails because the table already exists.
stages.expect: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM prices; returns 4 and SELECT COUNT(*) FROM seats; returns 8.

stages.title: Cost per department
steps: Join seats to prices on the SKU.
Sum the price per department, most expensive first.
Use a LEFT JOIN from prices to seats to find SKUs nobody uses.
Save both queries in report.sql.
hints: Unused means the seats side is NULL after the LEFT JOIN.
stages.expect: Cost per department: IT|136, Sales|66, Helpdesk|16. The unused SKU query returns E3.

stages.title: Show it on a page
steps: Create ~/megalab/ops/license-ledger/index.php.
Open licenses.db with PDO, exceptions on, associative fetch mode.
Run the cost-per-department query and loop the rows into an HTML table with columns Dept and Monthly cost.
Add a total line under the table.
Start the server with php -S localhost:8000 in the folder and open http://localhost:8000.
stages.expect: The page shows a 3-row table IT 136, Sales 66, Helpdesk 16 and a total of 218. The terminal logs a 200 for GET /.

title: Site status board
story: Noor in the NOC wants one screen that shows whether each Contoso site is fine. A Python check writes the data, a small web page shows it.
result: A Python checker that writes status.json and an HTML/CSS/JS board with coloured cards and a pulsing alert, served by Python.

stages.title: Write the checker
steps: Make ~/megalab/ops/site-status/ and create checks.csv with header host,disk_pct and rows GENT-SW1 62, BRUG-SW1 85, ANTW-FS1 93, HASS-SW1 40.
Create ~/megalab/ops/site-status/check.py with a function classify(pct) that returns ok below 80, warn below 90, otherwise down.
Read checks.csv with csv.DictReader and print host, pct and state for each row.
Test the edges by printing classify(79), classify(80) and classify(90).
hints: `int(row["disk_pct"])` because every CSV value arrives as text.
stages.expect: Four lines: GENT-SW1 62 ok, BRUG-SW1 85 warn, ANTW-FS1 93 down, HASS-SW1 40 ok. The edges give ok, warn, down.

stages.title: Save status.json
steps: Collect one dict per host with keys host, disk and state in a list.
Write the list to status.json with json.dump and indent=2.
Run check.py again and open status.json.
hints: `json.dump(data, f, indent=2)` inside a with-block opened with "w".
stages.expect: status.json is a list of 4 objects; the first is {"host": "GENT-SW1", "disk": 62, "state": "ok"}.

stages.title: Build the board
steps: Create ~/megalab/ops/site-status/index.html and ~/megalab/ops/site-status/style.css.
Add a header with the title Contoso sites and an empty main with id board.
Store your colours as custom properties on :root: --ok, --warn, --down.
Style main as a wrapping flex row of cards, each card at least 160px wide.
Add classes .ok, .warn and .down that set the card's left border colour.
hints: `flex: 1 1 160px` on the card, `flex-wrap: wrap` on the parent.
stages.expect: The page shows the header and an empty board area with no errors in the browser console.

stages.title: Fill it with fetch
steps: Create ~/megalab/ops/site-status/board.js and load it with defer.
Fetch status.json, await the JSON and build one card per host with the host name, disk % and the state as its class.
Serve the folder with python3 -m http.server 8000 and open http://localhost:8000.
hints: fetch does not work from file://, which is why you serve the folder.
stages.expect: Four cards: GENT-SW1 and HASS-SW1 green, BRUG-SW1 orange, ANTW-FS1 red. The server log shows GET /status.json 200.

stages.title: Make problems move
steps: Give every card a transition so it lifts 4px on hover.
Write @keyframes pulse that fades the box-shadow in and out.
Apply the pulse only to .down cards, running forever.
Change ANTW-FS1 to 70 in checks.csv, rerun check.py and reload the page.
stages.expect: Before the change only ANTW-FS1 pulses red. After the change no card pulses and all four are green except BRUG-SW1.

title: Onboarding intake
story: HR sends Contoso IT a messy list of new starters. You clean it with tested Python, then build a small PHP form so HR can add people straight into a database.
result: A git repo on a feature branch merged into main: a tested Python cleaner, a starters.db and a PHP intake form with validation.

stages.title: Branch for the feature
steps: Make ~/megalab/ops/onboarding-intake/, run git init and commit an empty README.md on main.
Add a .gitignore that ignores *.db and .venv/.
Create and switch to a branch called intake.
stages.expect: git branch shows * intake and main. git status lists .gitignore as untracked until you commit it.

stages.title: Clean the list
steps: Create ~/megalab/ops/onboarding-intake/raw.csv with header name,dept and 5 rows: ada with two spaces before and one after, it / BRAM,sales / lien with a space after, IT / an empty name, Sales / noor,helpdesk.

Create ~/megalab/ops/onboarding-intake/clean.py with a function clean(name, dept) that returns a dict with name in Title case, dept in UPPER case and upn as lowercase name + @contoso.com, or None when the name is blank.
Read raw.csv, keep only the rows that are not None and write them to starters.csv.
Print each cleaned row.
hints: A list comprehension with `if r is not None` drops the blanks.
Wrap the file read in try/except FileNotFoundError and print a clear message.
stages.expect: Four rows: Ada IT ada@contoso.com, Bram SALES bram@contoso.com, Lien IT lien@contoso.com, Noor HELPDESK noor@contoso.com. The blank row is gone.

stages.title: Test the cleaner
steps: Create a venv in .venv, activate it and pip install pytest.
Create ~/megalab/ops/onboarding-intake/test_clean.py with three tests: spaces are stripped, a blank name gives None, the upn is lowercase.
Run pytest.
stages.expect: pytest ends with 3 passed.

stages.title: Intake form in PHP
steps: Create ~/megalab/ops/onboarding-intake/schema.sql with table starters(name TEXT, dept TEXT, upn TEXT UNIQUE) and load it into starters.db with sqlite3.
Create ~/megalab/ops/onboarding-intake/index.php with a form (name, dept select IT/SALES/HELPDESK) that posts to itself.
On POST, trim the name, reject it if empty, build the upn and insert with a prepared statement.
Below the form, list every starter from the table.
Run php -S localhost:8000 and add Jonas in SALES.
stages.expect: After the POST the list shows Jonas SALES jonas@contoso.com. Submitting an empty name shows your error and adds nothing.

stages.title: Merge the feature
steps: Commit everything on intake (starters.db and .venv must not appear).
Switch to main and merge intake.
Show the graph of the history.
stages.expect: git status on main is clean, git ls-files shows no .db file and no .venv folder, and the log contains your intake commits.

title: Ship the ops portal
story: Contoso wants the site board as a real small app in a container, with a health check that a PowerShell script can test after every deploy, and the code on a remote.
result: A PHP front-controller app with / and /health routes in a Docker container, a pwsh smoke test, and the repo pushed to a remote branch.

stages.title: Front controller
steps: Create ~/megalab/ops/ops-portal/public/index.php as the only entry point and ~/megalab/ops/ops-portal/src/sites.php with a function that returns the 4 sites from status.json (copy it from site-status).
Route on the request path: / shows the site table, /health answers JSON, anything else answers 404.
The /health JSON has status ok and sites set to the number of sites.
Run php -S localhost:8000 -t public public/index.php and test with curl.
hints: `http_response_code(404);` before you print the not found text.
stages.expect: curl -s localhost:8000/health prints {"status":"ok","sites":4}. curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' localhost:8000/nope prints 404.

stages.title: Polish the table
steps: Add ~/megalab/ops/ops-portal/public/app.js loaded with defer.
When the page loads, animate each table row in from opacity 0 and translateY(8px) with element.animate, 60ms apart.
Animate only transform and opacity.
stages.expect: On reload the 4 rows slide in one after another and stay visible.

stages.title: Containerise it
steps: Create ~/megalab/ops/ops-portal/Dockerfile from php:8.3-cli that copies the app to /app and starts php -S 0.0.0.0:80 -t public public/index.php.
Build the image as ops-portal:1.
Run it detached with port 8080 on your Mac mapped to 80 in the container, named ops-portal.
Check it with curl and docker ps.
hints: If 8080 is taken, find the process with `lsof -i :8080`.
stages.expect: docker ps shows ops-portal with 0.0.0.0:8080->80/tcp and curl -s localhost:8080/health prints {"status":"ok","sites":4}.

stages.title: Smoke test script
steps: Create ~/megalab/ops/ops-portal/smoke.ps1 with a param $Url defaulting to http://localhost:8080 and Set-StrictMode -Version Latest.
Call $Url/health with Invoke-RestMethod inside try/catch.
Print PASS when status is ok and sites is 4, otherwise FAIL and exit 1.
Run it once with the container up and once after docker stop ops-portal.
stages.expect: With the container running: PASS. After stopping it: FAIL, and $LASTEXITCODE is 1.

stages.title: Push to a remote
steps: Commit the app on a branch called release-1.
Make a bare repo at ~/megalab/remotes/ops-portal.git with git init --bare and add it as origin.
Push release-1 and set its upstream.
Show the remote branches.
stages.expect: git branch -r lists origin/release-1 and git status says Your branch is up to date with 'origin/release-1'.
